rows.notes: The cited document is a narrative review of 16 ML-based irrigation scheduling studies (Abstract; Section 3; Data availability statement says no research data generated). It reports no own data or experiments. Statements about IoT/WSN enhancing data availability and real-time prediction (Introduction; Section 6) and about ML/IoT promoting productivity are drawn from the reviewed literature (e.g., Hunsaker et al. 2005; Kashyap et al. 2021), not from the authors' own results.

Review paper with no primary data. The 18-30% water saving figure is the review's summary of Alibabaei et al. (2022) (Section 3; Table 1), a DQN model run on LSTM-simulated environment, not remote sensing per se; the 'fully autonomous smart irrigation' statement refers to Goap et al. (2018). Remote-sensing integration is only proposed in Section 4.1 as a way to address data scarcity, not tested.

Review paper with no primary data. The productivity increase is the review's report of Alibabaei et al. (2022) results (Section 3), a simulation-based RL study, not the review authors' own finding; no remote sensing integration was tested in any reviewed study, it is only recommended in Section 4.1.

notes: Full text appears complete (Sections 1-7 plus references). The document is explicitly a literature review of 16 ML irrigation studies; all claimed effects are secondary reports of other authors' work, so Q1 is 'no' for every row.
